data.name: Antarda
data.detailed_description:
“Antarda” is a psychological horror where exploration, sound, and tension take priority over combat. You find yourself in an unsettling place that reacts to your actions and gradually distorts your perception of reality.

As you explore, you uncover fragments of a deeper story hidden within the environment, notes, and unfolding events that don’t always provide clear answers. The world is not static—it changes, observes, and responds, constantly creating a sense of uncertainty.

Gameplay focuses on exploration, environmental puzzle-solving, and survival in situations where caution and observation are your only tools. Sound and lighting play a crucial role in building tension, and every careless move can lead to unexpected consequences.

Will you manage to keep your grasp on reality before it begins to collapse?

data.short_description: Antarda is a psychological horror experience focused on exploration, sound, and tension over combat. Traverse unsettling environments, uncover fragmented story pieces, and survive in a place that reacts to you. Every step triggers events. Can you trust what you see or hear before reality collapses?

content_descriptors.notes:
Content Warning / Mature Content Description

This game contains themes that may be disturbing to some players. It includes psychological horror elements such as intense atmosphere, tension, and fear-based scenarios. Players may encounter depictions of violence, implied violence, and disturbing imagery presented in a horror context.

The game may also feature unsettling sound design, sudden loud noises, and jump scares intended to create stress and discomfort. Some environments and narrative elements include dark themes such as isolation, mental distress, and loss of control over reality.

There is no focus on sexual content, sexual violence, drug abuse, or self-harm as gameplay elements, however certain story or environmental references may touch on mature psychological themes.

Player discretion is advised.
